title: Filter on JSON timestamps in SQL before LIMIT, and regex-guard the cast
answers: how to compare sync_type_config.last_full_run_at in a queryset
Postgres error casting JSON string to timestamp
why not filter stalled schemas in Python after the query
naive timestamp read in session timezone
body:
Convention seen in `products/warehouse_sources/backend/stalled_schedules.py:stalled_schema_queryset`: `sync_type_config.last_full_run_at` is free-form JSON. Before casting it, check it with `When(sync_type_config__last_full_run_at__regex=_AWARE_ISO_TIMESTAMP, then=Cast(KeyTextTransform(...), DateTimeField()))` and default to NULL. Without that guard, Postgres raises on a string it cannot parse and reads a naive stamp in the session zone, which invents freshness. The SQL guard mirrors the Python rule in `ExternalDataSchema.last_full_run`: accept only ISO stamps with an offset or Z.
Do the filtering in SQL so the sweep and repair command can keep their `LIMIT`. Filtering in Python after the LIMIT let excluded rows fill every slot. Filtering in Python before it loaded every candidate on each hourly sweep.
Tests: `test_an_unusable_run_stamp_falls_back_to_the_sync_stamp` (unparseable and naive cases) and `find_stalled_schemas(limit=1)` with the excluded row sorted first.
applies: Django querysets in warehouse_sources that compare timestamps stored inside the sync_type_config JSON
